text:
Faye (Docs): Quick thread to land a small PR that clarifies the "tenant tiers" -> SLA mapping in Dedicated docs and to add a concrete canary rollout example for capacity migration. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/2799
Omar (Platform): Nice. We should be explicit about semantics: "tenant tier" labels (standard, isolated, reserved) map to different isolation guarantees — e.g., isolated = process+VM isolation; reserved = scheduling isolation + capacity reservation.
Faye (Docs): added a concise mapping paragraph under "Isolation & SLAs" with non-technical wording and links to the architecture page.
June (SRE): One practical note: include a troubleshooting bullet for cross-tenant noisy neighbors — how to check per-tenant CPU/GPU steal and route-level rate limits. Keep it short, link to /observability/tenant-metrics.
Faye (Docs): added the bullet. Also found a broken reference: docs used /internal/sla/matrix which CI flagged.
ci-bot: Link check failed: /internal/sla/matrix -> 404 (found in docs/dedicated/isolation.md line ~58)
Omar (Platform): That internal page moved to /guides/sla-and-tiers; update to that.
Faye (Docs): updated the link, pushed commit. Also included a simple YAML example showing how to tag a pool with a tier and the SLA label for terraform and the Console UI snippet. Terraform example uses var `pool_tier = "isolated"`.
Kai (SDK): Heads up: the rollout SDK snippet still uses the old `rollout_strategy` name. Our current param is `rolloutMode` and values are case-sensitive (e.g., 'Canary'). Also normalize `batch_limit` usage in the example.
Faye (Docs): fixed the SDK samples (both python/js) to `rolloutMode='Canary'` and `batch_limit`. Added a small runnable canary snippet showing traffic percentages and a small wait/check loop.
Faye (Docs): new Python snippet added in PR:
```python
from redwood import Client
client = Client()
# canary rollout example: 10% -> 50% -> 100%
resp = client.rollout_update(pool_id='pool-xyz', rolloutMode='Canary', steps=[{'percent':10,'duration_sec':300},{'percent':50,'duration_sec':600}])
print('started canary', resp.id)
```
Kai (SDK): Looks good. Suggest adding a short note: "Canary traffic is route-level; ensure route-level rate limits allow initial percent or you'll surface 429s."
June (SRE): Also add an on-prem/VPC note: when migrating capacity with canary, use lower initial percent (<=5%) for small GPU clusters to avoid cache thrash. Recommend terraform var example: `initial_canary_percent = 5` for on-prem.
Faye (Docs): added the on-prem recommendation and a tiny terraform var snippet. Also fixed a typo in the SLA table header (was "sla_tier" -> should be "tier_sla").
Marta (PM): From product POV, please include a user-facing sentence: "Reserved pools offer the strongest uptime guarantee; isolated pools prioritize tenant separation." Short and non-technical.
Faye (Docs): added Marta's line under the quick intro.
Omar (Platform): One more internal nit: in the terraform example we reference `min_replicas` but some older repos still use `replica_min`. Add a short migration note and a small mapping table.
Faye (Docs): added a tiny migration table (old -> new var name) and a link to the migration guide. Filed issue #589 to add automated snippet smoke tests so SDK param regressions get caught.
ci-bot: Link check and lint queued
ci-bot: All checks passed for PR #2799 (link-check, lint, mdspell)
Faye (Docs): Merged after green CI. Follow-ups: (1) add a short dashboard screenshot for tenant metrics (issue #590), (2) author a worked example showing a full capacity migration with canary (issue #591). Closing thread, thanks everyone :sparkles:
